tiers.criteria: Line coverage >= 90% AND branch coverage >= 80% for the target module.
Line coverage 75-89% AND branch coverage 65-79%.
Line coverage 60-74% OR branch coverage 50-64%.
Line coverage 40-59%. Major code paths untested.
Line coverage < 40%. Only trivial happy-path tested.

Every test has specific, meaningful assertions (exact value checks, not just 'no exception'). Asserts cover return values, state changes, side effects, AND error conditions. Uses appropriate assertion methods.
Good assertions covering return values and error conditions. Minor gaps in side-effect verification.
Assertions present but some are weak (assert result is not None instead of checking actual value). Error conditions partially tested.
Many tests just check 'no exception raised'. Few meaningful value assertions.
Trivial assertions only (assert True, assert response.status_code == 200 without body checks).

Tests cover: empty inputs, boundary values (min/max), error conditions (invalid input, not found, permission denied), concurrent operations (if applicable), and at least 2 non-obvious edge cases specific to the business logic.
Tests cover most common edge cases (empty input, not found, permission). 1 non-obvious case.
Some edge cases covered but gaps in error conditions or boundary values.
Only happy path + 1-2 obvious error cases (e.g., 404).
Happy path only. No edge cases.
All tests pass individually and in any order. Proper setup/teardown. Each test tests one thing. Clear naming pattern. Tests use existing conftest.py fixtures.
Tests independent and structured. Minor issues.
Mostly independent but some shared mutable state or order dependencies.
Test isolation issues: shared state, order-dependent tests.
Tests tightly coupled, can't run individually, or fragile.
Follows existing test patterns: uses pytest, uses conftest fixtures, follows file naming (test_<module>.py), uses existing test client and DB fixtures, consistent mock patterns.
Mostly follows conventions. 1 minor deviation.
Partially follows conventions. Uses pytest but doesn't leverage existing fixtures.
Uses different testing patterns (e.g., unittest.TestCase when repo uses pytest functions).
Completely different testing style. Ignores existing test infrastructure.

agent_prompt_template:
You are given a Python FastAPI codebase at /repo. Your task is to write comprehensive tests for a specific module.

## Module Under Test
{module_under_test}

## Implementation Files
The code to test is in:
{implementation_files}

## Target Test File
Write your tests to: {test_target_file}

## Existing Test Patterns
{existing_test_patterns}

## Instructions
1. Study the existing test patterns in the repo (conftest.py, other test files)
2. Write comprehensive tests covering:
   - All happy-path flows
   - Edge cases and boundary conditions
   - Error conditions (invalid input, unauthorized access, resource not found)
   - State transitions and side effects
3. Follow existing test conventions exactly
4. Use existing fixtures from conftest.py
5. Each test should test one thing with clear, specific assertions
